state: Can compiles checked IR to TypeScript executed directly by pinned Bun 1.4.2. Qualification observed that native Error.stack reports original TypeScript coordinates after Bun transpilation but ignores an external Can-to-TS sourceMappingURL. Accessing a native Error own stack data descriptor caused no name/message getter calls in the probe; proxies and accessor stacks must still be rejected. I40 requires exact Can spans for nested calls, async callbacks and Unicode columns, upstream encoding, failed publication for malformed/missing maps, and diagnostics without machine paths, source content, credentials or native messages. Go owns IR byte spans and UTF16 conversion. Consider: feed explicit compiler segments to bundled gen-mapping, validate maps, and trace the Bun-reported TS frames through bundled trace-mapping; rely only on Bun's automatic mapping despite this result; or emit only catch-origin labels without consuming stack maps. The first choice retains checked nearest-span origins for primitive or synthetic frames and outputs only source-index-admitted locations. Runtime sources and source index are verified generation artifacts; no authored source content is embedded. No trace stack implementation has been completed yet.

design.instructions: Which approach meets this mapping and diagnostic contract given the runtime evidence?

criteria.trace: Encode Go segments with bundled gen-mapping and trace Bun TS stack positions with bundled trace-mapping; supplement with checked origins and sanitize by the source index.
criteria.bun: Rely entirely on Bun to compose the external Can map automatically.
criteria.origin: Report catch origins only and do not consume stack source maps.
